{{FA|January 1, 2011}}
[[File:Another Crystal.jpg|right|250px|thumb|Artwork depicting the crystals from ''Final Fantasy IV''.]]
{{Quote|Take a good look. Isn't it beautiful? It's the original crystal... This is where it all began... The birthplace of all things...|[[Kuja]]}}
'''Crystals''' {{j|クリスタル|Kurisutaru}}, also called '''orbs''' and '''spheres''', are legendary and often [[Element (term)|elemental]] objects that have appeared in every game in the main [[Final Fantasy series|''Final Fantasy'' series]]. Even in games where they are not a central plot point, there has been at least some reference to them. Crystals often have power over natural phenomena and function as a powerful source of magical energy. Many antagonists focus their efforts on seizing the crystals to gain power towards their goal.

{{See|Dark Crystal (term)|Earth Crystal (term)|Fire Crystal (term)|Water Crystal (term)|Wind Crystal (term)}}
{{See|Crystallization}}

== Profile ==
The original set up was to have four elemental crystals: a [[Water Crystal (term)|Water Crystal]], a [[Fire Crystal (term)|Fire Crystal]], a [[Wind Crystal (term)|Wind Crystal]], and an [[Earth Crystal (term)|Earth Crystal]]. On some occasions, crystals may be aligned with [[Dark Crystal (term)|Darkness]]. Crystals are often found in [[crystal room]]s in early games. The crystals are often treasured for their power and many myths and legends surround the true extent of their abilities. Uncovering the truth of these myths and their meaning is a typical part of a ''Final Fantasy'' game.

The concept of the four elemental crystals that sustain the world likely derives from the [[wikipedia:Five elements (Japanese philosophy)|Japanese five elements philosophy]]. These five elements are, in ascending order of power: Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, and Void. The element of Void is not represented as a crystal, but may have taken the form of [[The Void (term)|The Void]], a dimension that connects the different [[Final Fantasy worlds|''Final Fantasy'' worlds]].

The concept of four elemental crystals that sustain the world was largely phased out since ''[[Final Fantasy V]]'', with crystals gaining more varied roles. Crystals remain as a source of life energy in some way and often act as a source of [[Magic (term)|magic]], sometimes powering [[Airship (term)|airships]] and other apparatus. Crystals contain within themselves both light and dark in that they have been used for both good and evil purposes. [[Summoned monsters]] are often bound to a crystal and the one possessing the crystal shard becomes able to summon the creature. The power of the crystal is often to transcend space and time and [[afterlife|life and death]], even allowing travel to other eras, worlds, and dimensions.

The crystal can be sentient and communicate with a chosen party, often via a mental link. Crystals choosing the player party as the "[[Warriors of Light]]" is a recurring theme in the early series, where the crystal, sensing that the world is in danger, tasks a band of warriors with the mission of saving it. The crystal lends the group its powers, often resulting in the party becoming able to use magic and other special abilities.

== Appearances ==
=== ''[[Final Fantasy]]'' ===
[[File:FFI PSP Crystal.png|right|75px|A Crystal (PSP).]]
Crystals were initially known as "Orbs" in the North American localization, due to a truncated Japanese-to-English translation.

The [[Warriors of Light]] begin in possession of four elemental crystals and each of the [[Four Fiends (Final Fantasy)|Four Fiends]] guards a larger, power-drained crystal of his or her own element, which the Warriors restore after defeating the Fiend. [[Garland (Final Fantasy)|Garland]] possesses a fifth "Dark Crystal", though its significance is not elaborated upon. When the Warriors of Light restore the light to the four crystals, they channel their energy into the fifth crystal, allowing them to [[Time travel|travel to the past]] to break the time loop.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy II]]'' ===
A [[Crystal Rod (Final Fantasy II)|Crystal Rod]] is a key item that unlocks the entrance to the [[Mysidian Tower]], where the ultimate magic, [[Ultima Tome (Final Fantasy II)|Ultima Tome]], is sealed. Atop the tower are four crystal orbs that represent each element.

When examined, the four blue crystals boost a specific stat of a random [[party]] member (including [[Richard Highwind|Ricard]]) by 10. If the randomized party member has maxed out in the stat, then nothing will happen. In the bottom-left is the crystal of power, which increases Strength. The top-left is the crystal of spirit, which increases Spirit. The top-right is the crystal of intelligence, which increase Intelligence. The bottom-right is the crystal of speed, which increases Agility. In the ''[[Final Fantasy Origins|Origins]]'' version, the [[Memo File]] and [[soft reset]] features allow a player to control who gets the stat gains by resetting until it chooses the desired character.

In the center of the room where the crystals lay is a fifth crystal that is orange, the crystal of the forbidden spell that contains the Ultima Tome that teaches [[Magic (Final Fantasy II)#Ultima|Ultima]].

In the [[bonus dungeon]] introduced in ''[[Final Fantasy I & II: Dawn of Souls|Dawn of Souls]]'', [[Soul of Rebirth]], the crystals grant [[Minwu (Final Fantasy II)|Minwu]] access to the Ultima Tome in [[Machanon]].

=== ''[[Final Fantasy III]]'' ===
[[File:Crystal Dome prologue artwork for Final Fantasy III 3D.png|thumb|right|Artwork by [[Akihiko Yoshida]].]]
There are eight crystals scattered across the world. Four exist on the Light World and four are found in the [[World of Darkness (Final Fantasy III)|World of Darkness]]. [[Xande (Final Fantasy III)|Xande]] is trying to drain them of their power to create an imbalance between light and darkness. He drains the crystals on the surface world, covering it in darkness and freezing time, but is unable to drain the ones on the floating continent. Eventually, the forces of darkness drain the other two crystals, creating an imbalance that summons the [[Cloud of Darkness (Final Fantasy III)|Cloud of Darkness]]. The Wind Crystal chooses four children to go out, restore the balance, and give the crystals back their power.

After the four youths find each crystal, they are given new [[Final Fantasy III jobs|job classes]]. Once the youths are given the powers of the four crystals of light, they enter the [[World of Darkness (Final Fantasy III)|World of Darkness]] and must defeat the four guardians of the dark crystals to obtain the aid of the [[Warriors of Darkness]]. They use the four crystals of darkness to make the Cloud of Darkness vulnerable.

Another crystal is found in [[Goldor Manor]], but it is a crystal made of pure gold as with everything that [[Goldor (Final Fantasy III)|Goldor]] owns. The Warriors of the Light initially suspect that the gold crystal is the Earth Crystal, but are mistaken, and the gold crystal has no special powers.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy IV]]'' ===
[[File:FF4 PSP Light Crystal.gif|left]]
[[File:FF4 PSP Dark Crystal.gif|right]]
There are eight primary Crystals. The four elemental Crystals form the "Light Crystals" and are kept in the [[Blue Planet (Final Fantasy IV)#Overworld|Overworld]]: The Crystal of Water is in [[Mysidia (Final Fantasy IV)|Mysidia]], the Crystal of Fire is in [[Damcyan]], the Crystal of Wind is in [[Fabul]], and the Crystal of Earth is in [[Troia]].

There are also four "Dark Crystals" kept in the [[Blue Planet (Final Fantasy IV)#Underworld|Underworld]]. The location of two of these Crystals is never revealed, but one is kept by the [[dwarf|dwarves]] in [[Dwarven Castle|their castle]] and one is found in the [[Sealed Cave (Final Fantasy IV)|Sealed Cave]].

If all eight Crystals are gathered in the [[Tower of Babil (Final Fantasy IV)|Tower of Babil]], it has been told that the "way to the [[Red Moon (Final Fantasy IV)|Moon]]" would open. Gathering the Crystals would actually summon the [[Giant of Babil]], an enormous, autonomous robot war machine. The [[Lunarian]] [[Zemus]] wants to have the giant destroy the [[Blue Planet (Final Fantasy IV)|Blue Planet]] so that the Lunarians could settle there and he uses [[Golbez]] to do so. Many more Crystals are revealed later, such as the eight Crystals of the Moon and a Crystal that appears in the battle with [[Zeromus (Final Fantasy IV)|Zeromus]].

The Crystals of the Moon are sentient and responsible for sealing Zemus' power for the time being. The Crystal that appears in the battle against Zemus is an item said to make Zeromus vulnerable. Golbez tried to use it, but only those born out of the Light can do so. When [[Cecil Harvey]] uses it, Zeromus becomes vulnerable and Cecil and his friends defeat it.

The Crystal of Flight rests within the ''[[Lunar Whale]]'' and is used to transport the heroes to the Moon and back. The [[Elder of Mysidia]] implies that crystals power the ''Lunar Whale'' and, in the 3D remake, several crystals are embedded in parts of the airship.

In the 3D remakes, each of the eight Crystals are colored differently. In the 2D releases, the crystals are light blue or dark red/black, depending on their alignment to Light or Darkness.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy IV -Interlude-]]'' ====
[[File:IV Interlude Crystal.png|right|thumb|Dark Crystal in the introduction.]]
Three crystals make an appearance, silently shedding their light within their chambers. The three crystals are the Fire Crystal in [[Damcyan]], the Wind Crystal of [[Fabul]], and the Dark Crystal inside the [[Sealed Cave (Final Fantasy IV)|Sealed Cave]].

==== ''[[Final Fantasy IV: The After Years]]'' ====
The [[Maenad|Mysterious Girl]] and [[Dark Kain|Kain?]] band to collect the eight crystals of the Blue Planet, all of which have returned to their original resting spots since Zeromus was defeated. The girl returns to the [[Red Moon (Final Fantasy IV)|Red Moon]] and drains the power of their crystals, shattering them.

In the depths of the [[True Moon]], numerous crystals appear and shatter, reviving various [[boss]]es from ''Final Fantasy IV'' to attack the party as they travel deeper into the moon. In the final chambers, the party recovers the eight crystals of the Blue Planet and, in the final battle with the [[Creator (The After Years)|Creator]], they are used to render him vulnerable to the party's attacks.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy V]]'' ===
{{Quote|Fire, Water, Wind, Earth. The peace and prosperity of the world is thanks to the power of these crystals. However...that power is nearing its limit. Not far off is the day when the wind slows...the water stills...and the earth trembles and quakes...and yet, everyone remains blissfully unaware...and the grave secret hidden within the crystals remain untold...|Intro}}
[[File:FF5Crystal.gif|right|A Crystal.]]
Four crystals control the elements in [[Bartz's world]] and, without them, the wind would not blow, the oceans would dry up, the fire would burn out, and the life of the earth would be destroyed. The Wind Crystal is kept in the [[Wind Shrine (Final Fantasy V)|Wind Shrine]] and maintained by [[Castle Tycoon|Tycoon]]. The Water Crystal is kept in the [[Walse Tower]] and maintained by [[Walse]]. The Fire Crystal is kept in [[Karnak]] and the Earth Crystal is located in the [[Ronka Ruins]]. Thirty years ago, the [[Warriors of Dawn]] used the power of the crystals to seal the malevolent warlock [[Exdeath]] within [[Exdeath's sealed cave|a cave]] where the power of the four crystals gathered.

[[Cid Previa]] invented a machine to amplify the crystals' output, but if the crystals were allowed to operate at this capacity, they would shatter. Cid regrets creating the machine. Exdeath tries to shatter the Crystals himself to be freed by using his spirit to [[Enthrallment|possess others]] to accomplish the deed. As the Wind Crystal shatters, it brands the four who had arrived at its shrine trying to save it as the Warriors of Light, tasked with protecting the crystals and, thus, the world. Despite their efforts, the crystals shatter one by one, with each shard becoming the source for a new [[Final Fantasy V jobs|job class]] for the Light Warriors as the crystals' will to bestow their power to the four so that they could vanquish Exdeath.

After the crystals are gone, [[Galuf Halm Baldesion]], one of the Light Warriors, returns to [[Galuf's world|his world]] on a [[Meteorite (Final Fantasy V)|meteorite]]. It is revealed that there exists a parallel world from where Exdeath originally emerged and the Dawn Warriors had sealed him into the other world to protect their own. After Exdeath was freed when the crystals shattered, he fled back to his own world and Galuf and the others follow suit, ready to continue the battle.

They find [[Crystal (Final Fantasy V boss)|Galuf's world's crystals]] guarding the [[Great Forest of Moore]], but are tricked by Exdeath into breaking their seals and he absconds with them. Galuf perishes in the battle against Exdeath and his role as a Light Warrior is taken up by his granddaughter, [[Krile Mayer Baldesion]]. The Light Warriors infiltrate [[Castle Exdeath]], but Exdeath destroys the crystals and the Light Warriors mysteriously find themselves in a new, [[merged world]].

It becomes apparent that both worlds [[Final Fantasy V world|were once one]]. A thousand years ago, a sorcerer named [[Enuo (Final Fantasy V)|Enuo]] had tried to destroy the world with the power of [[Void (Final Fantasy V)|the Void]], a mysterious pure energy, and the world's crystals had been split to seal the entrance to the Void between the worlds. When the crystals that sustained the world were split, the world itself was split in two, but after Exdeath had the crystals of both worlds destroyed, the worlds merged once again. The portal to the [[Interdimensional Rift (Final Fantasy V)|Interdimensional Rift]] manifests as a result and Exdeath enters it, gaining the ability to wield the power of the Void.

The Light Warriors follow Exdeath to the Rift and defeat him, despite him being transformed by the Void into [[Neo Exdeath (Final Fantasy V)|Neo Exdeath]], a being that seeks the world's destruction. Left hovering in the Void in the battle's aftermath, the Light Warriors learn that the crystals that sustain their world were once born from the Void, creating life. The crystals are reborn with the power of the two generations of Warriors of Dawn, regenerating the world. The Void disappears and the Light Warriors return to their realm. The four rendezvous a year later and decide to continue protecting the crystals and, thus, the world, together.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy: Legend of the Crystals]]'' ====
[[File:LotC Crystals.JPG|right|thumb|The Water, Fire, and Earth Crystals.]]
[[Ra Devil]]'s forces have stolen the crystals of Earth, Fire, and Water. Sensing that something is amiss, [[Linaly]]'s grandfather sends her to check on the Wind Crystal. The spirit of [[Mid Previa]] had been residing in this crystal and uses Linaly's body to hide the crystal from Ra Devil's forces.

Linaly is captured and later rescued by [[Prettz]], [[Valkus]], and [[Rouge]]. The other three crystals are reclaimed, but not before Ra Devil had already transformed himself using their power.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy VI]]'' ===
[[File:Magicite.PNG|right|Magicite]]
When an [[Esper (Final Fantasy VI)|esper]] dies, its remains crystallize into [[Magicite (Final Fantasy VI)|magicite]] that appear as glowing shards of green crystal. In contrast to magic extracted from live espers via [[magitek]], [[Magic (Final Fantasy VI command)|magic]] can be taught naturally and at a much higher potency using magicite.

Using magicite, the [[Returners]] wield magic to fight the [[Gestahlian Empire]] on its own terms for a time before the [[Battle of Vector|empire is decimated by the espers]]. The empire abandons magitek in favor of magicite in preparation to invade the [[Esper World|esper homeworld]] and seize the [[Warring Triad (Final Fantasy VI)|Warring Triad]], a trio of petrified [[Divinity in Final Fantasy|deities]]. After the imperial general and [[Magitek Knight|magitek knight]] [[Kefka Palazzo|Kefka]] revives the Warring Triad and absorbs their powers, he becomes the source of all magic in the world. Thus, upon his defeat, espers, magicite, and magic disappear.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy VII]]'' ===
[[File:ObservatoryHG.jpg|thumb|right|The four Huge Materia.]]
The crystallized form of [[Mako]] is known as [[Materia (Final Fantasy VII)|Materia]] and is a nod to the crystals of past. The Materia allow the user to control [[Magic (Final Fantasy VII)|magic spells]], [[Summon (Final Fantasy VII)|summons]], gives boosts to statistics, and adds extra commands. Two exceptionally powerful Materia pieces are the [[White Materia]] and [[Black Materia (Final Fantasy VII)|Black Materia]]. [[Sephiroth]] seeks the Black Materia to summon [[Meteor (Final Fantasy VII)|Meteor]] to strike the [[Planet (Final Fantasy VII)|Planet]], while [[Aerith Gainsborough|Aeris]] tries to stop him by using the White Materia to summon [[Holy (Final Fantasy VII)|Holy]], the ultimate White Magic spell.

There are also four rare natural Materia found in [[Materia Cave]]s: [[Knights of Round (Final Fantasy VII)|Knights of Round]], [[Mime (Final Fantasy VII)|Mime]], [[HP↔MP (Final Fantasy VII)|HP↔MP]], and [[Quadra Magic]], said to be so powerful due to being in secluded areas and have been given time to grow and collect. There are also the four [[Huge Materia (Final Fantasy VII)|Huge Materia]], colors red, blue, yellow, and green. Three of the four Huge Materia correspond to matching color Materia: [[Master Summon (Final Fantasy VII)|Master Summon]], [[Master Command]], and [[Master Magic]] can be acquired from the red, yellow, and green Huge Materia if the player has mastered all Materia shards of that type. The Huge Materia's appearance is of homage to the elemental crystals of the early series.

==== ''[[Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-]]'' ====
[[File:CrisisCoreCrystals.PNG|thumb|left|The Materia summoned by Sephiroth.]]
During the first battle with him at the [[Nibel Reactor]], [[Sephiroth (Crisis Core boss)|Sephiroth]] can summon four colored crystals to assist him. The crystals are identical in appearance to the four Huge Materia from ''Final Fantasy VII''.

In a locked chamber in the [[Banora Underground]], [[Zack Fair]] can enter battle with [[Green Materia (enemy)|Green Materia]], [[Red Materia (enemy)|Red Materia]], [[Yellow Materia (enemy)|Yellow Materia]], and [[Blue Materia (enemy)|Blue Materia]]. They cast elemental magic and their coloring corresponds to four of the five typical Materia colors. The Banora Underground caves are full of crystals due to their proximity to the [[Lifestream]]. The Goddess Materia is a large natural Materia that [[Genesis Rhapsodos]] seeks to cure his [[degradation]].

Zack can also equip Materia for various effects in battle.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy VIII]]'' ===
[[File:Lunatic Pandora Crystal Pillar FFVIII Art.jpg|right|thumb|150px|The crystal pillar.]]
The [[Crystal Pillar (Final Fantasy VIII)|crystal pillar]] is a gigantic crystal believed to have originated from the [[Moon (Final Fantasy VIII)|Moon]]. The [[Monster (term)#Final Fantasy VIII|monsters]] in the world originate from the moon and the crystal is responsible for summoning them to the planet by creating a strong energy field. It reacts to a certain location on the planet, creating a signal that directs the [[Lunar Cry (Final Fantasy VIII)|Lunar Cry]] towards it. Thus, the crystal acts as a malevolent force.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy IX]]'' ===
{{Main|Crystal (Final Fantasy IX)}}
[[File:CrystalWorld-5-ffix.png|thumb|The original crystal in the [[Crystal World]].]]
The crystal is the origin of life in the universe, marking a new iteration on the series' use of crystals as the force that sustains the game worlds. ''Final Fantasy IX'' calls back to many aspects of the early series and the crystal represents the origin and interconnectedness of all life.

The term "crystal" may refer to the planets' individual crystals or the "original crystal" at the [[Crystal World]]. Though the planets' crystals are mainly represented in abstractions and the Crystal World crystal only appears briefly, the crystal is one of the game's [[Final Fantasy IX#Themes|main motifs that ties up the main theme of life and death]] and appears in its [[Logos of Final Fantasy|logo art]].

Small gemstones also feature as [[Final Fantasy IX jewels|consumable items]] and [[Add-on (Final Fantasy IX)|accessories]] and house the essences of [[Eidolon (Final Fantasy IX)|eidolons]].{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy X]]'' ===
[[File:Crystal Trophy-render-ffx.png|left|65px|The crystal trophy in Luca.]]
[[Sphere (Final Fantasy X)|Spheres]] are round crystalline objects used for various purposes in the world of [[Spira]]. They contain various magical energies provided by the [[Pyrefly|pyreflies]] embedded in them, allowing them to act as keys, contain memories, and even record events that can be viewed [[Movie sphere|like a movie]]. They also symbolically represent the game's theme of cycles.

Just prior to the series of [[final boss|final boss fights]], [[Tidus]] and company are warped to a bizarre spinning room called "Sin - The Nucleus". Within the Nucleus, Tidus must avoid crystal spikes while grabbing ten glowing, teleporting crystals, each of which bestows either powerful spheres or weapons. Once all ten items are acquired, the player is teleported to [[Inside Sin|Dream's End]] for the final battle.

A larger crystal appears in [[Luca (Final Fantasy X)|Luca]]. There is a statue in the round square where a clear crystal is sitting. As the player walks closer, the camera focuses on the crystal. The Crystal Cup is handed to the [[Besaid Aurochs]] by [[Wakka]] if the team wins the [[blitzball]] tournament.

When the [[Magus Sisters (Final Fantasy X)|Magus Sisters]] perform [[Delta Attack (ability)|Delta Attack]], they surround the enemy party in eight crystals, four of blue hue and four of red-orange hue. This refers to ''Final Fantasy IV'', where there were four blue crystals of the surface world and four red-orange crystals of the Underground.{{clear}}

==== ''[[Final Fantasy X-2]]'' ====
[[Dressphere]]s allow one to use the memories within the sphere to unleash associated powers.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy XI]]'' ===
{{Main|Crystal (Final Fantasy XI)|Mothercrystal (Final Fantasy XI)}}[[File:Crystal FFXI.jpg|thumb|right|The [[Seed Crystal]] in ''Final Fantasy XI: A Crystalline Prophecy''.]]Crystals play an important role in almost every story in Final Fantasy XI. They also have several gameplay uses, such as battlefield entry points and items used for crafting. All of the crystals are shards broken off from the original great crystal, which brought the world into existence. This great crystal split into 5 great shards, now called mothercrystals. These mothercrystals now stud the land of Vana'diel and grant life to the denizens.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy XII]]'' ===
[[File:FF12 Sun Cryst Model.png|right|95px|The Sun Cryst.]]
Crystals are commonly found in the form of magicite. [[Magicite#Final Fantasy XII|Magicite]], in the world of [[Ivalice (Final Fantasy XII)|Ivalice]], is described as a kind of magickal stone, capable of storing [[Mist (Final Fantasy XII)|Mist]] and being extracted for its use in magick. [[Nethicite]] is a special type of magicite that holds great amounts of magickal energy. Items such as the [[Dawn Shard]] are revealed to be shards of the [[Sun-Cryst]], a large crystal and a powerful form of nethicite, having been used in the conquests and campaigns of the legendary Dynast-King [[Raithwall]] of the [[Dalmasca (Final Fantasy XII)|Kingdom of Dalmasca]] that has secured his legacy for centuries.

Through the studies of [[Cidolfus Demen Bunansa|Dr. Cid]], the [[Archadia|Archadian Empire]] has begun to synthesize artificial nethicite and, with it, the Archadians have begun a campaign to conquer the world. [[Ashelia B'nargin Dalmasca|Princess Ashe]] focuses much of her efforts on acquiring a shard of the Sun-Cryst to use as power to wage war on Archadia, while the Archadians track down the same shards for experimentation.

[[File:Save crystal.jpg|thumb|A Save Crystal.]]
Crystals are found throughout the world and one of their many functions is as a [[save point]]. These Crystals are divided into save crystals, which let the player save the game, and gate crystals, which also allow teleportation to other gate crystals. Many enemies also [[Item drop|drop]] various elemental crystals, used for making items in the [[Bazaar (Final Fantasy XII)|Bazaar]]. [[Esper (Final Fantasy XII)|Espers]] are also bound to crystals before they are defeated.

There is also an enemy that takes the form of a crystal called a [[Crystalbug (red)|Crystalbug]].

The [[Great Crystal (Final Fantasy XII)|Great Crystal]] is a gargantuan crystal and speculated by the party to be the origin of Mist in Ivalice. This is where the [[Occuria]] dwell. Occuria themselves resemble living crystals and are said to be immortal.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy XII: Revenant Wings]]'' ====
Crystals come in the form of [[auracite]], which people can use to summon [[Esper (Revenant Wings)|Yarhi]]. Using the auracite comes with a price: each time someone uses it, their [[Anima (Revenant Wings)|anima]] slowly drains away. This is the reason why the [[aegyl]] have been reduced to emotionless shells.

There are also larger pieces of crystals called [[Auralith]]s from which all auracite come. Destroying the Auraliths releases the trapped anima that they have absorbed. The [[Soul Crystal (Revenant Wings)|Soul Crystal]] gameplay element in certain battles reincarnates its team's [[Knocked Out|KO'd]] members periodically.

=== ''[[Fortress]]'' ===
[[File:Fortress - Auraliths?.jpg|thumb|200px|Unknown Crystal-like objects.]]
Crystal-like objects appeared in concepts and came in eight different (apparently elemental) types. It is unknown whether these objects were nethicite, auracite, Auralith, or something else entirely.{{clear}}

===''[[Final Fantasy XIII]]''===
[[File:Hopesummons.jpg|thumb|right|[[Hope Estheim|Hope]] uses his eidolith to summon his Eidolon.]]
Crystals interact in the world in the form of [[fal'Cie]], [[Divinity in Final Fantasy|god]]-like machines powered by the crystals. Their power seems limitless as they helped create [[Cocoon (Final Fantasy XIII)|Cocoon]], which is essentially another moon of the world of [[Gran Pulse]]. These entities can create [[l'Cie]] by planting a crystal shard, known as an [[eidolith]], somewhere inside the human body; the l'Cie are, to a degree, their avatars in the world.

L'Cie can use magic and summon [[Eidolon (Final Fantasy XIII)|Eidolons]] via their eidoliths. If the l'Cie fails in the [[Focus (Fabula Nova Crystallis)|task they are given]], the power of the crystals will turn them into a monstrous crystallized [[Cie'th]]. If they complete their Focus, l'Cie are rewarded with eternity by [[crystal stasis|becoming lifeless crystals]]. Because both fates are considered to be a fate akin to (or even worse than) death, Cocoon citizens live in fear of the l'Cie and cast out those who become as such.

Humans, like the fal'Cie, also possess crystal power, though in a different manner. Crystal is the universe's life substance. The crystals power the fal'Cie like a computer's processor, giving them amazing magical powers and making them immortal, incapable of aging, yet the humans possess an even greater power; when a human dies, their [[Soul (Fabula Nova Crystallis)|soul]] turns into crystal energy and passes through the [[Etro's gate|Door of Souls]] to be eventually reborn. The fal'Cie envy this trait as they, too, would like to pass through the Door of Souls to be reunited with their [[Maker]]. During the game's final chapters, the party can observe the crystal energy in the air as tiny glimmering shards.

====''[[Final Fantasy XIII-2]]''====
[[File:Monster crystal.jpg|thumb|Monster turns into a crystal.]]
When [[Noel Kreiss|Noel]] and [[Serah Farron|Serah]] defeat a monster in battle, they can [[Paradigm Pack|gain its power]] in form of [[Crystallization|crystal]] and summon it to fight alongside them. This ability was granted to Serah by the goddess [[Etro]]. [[Mog (Final Fantasy XIII-2)|Mog]] has a crystal on his antenna instead of the classic [[moogle]] pompom; it is also incorporated into the [[Final Fantasy XIII-2 weapons|weapons]] he turns into.

[[Fragment]]s, crystallized memories, take appearance of various crystals and [[Artefact (Final Fantasy XIII-2)|artefacts]], items that do not belong in their time period, are also a type of crystal. [[Caius Ballad|Caius']] greatsword and armor have a crystal attached to them, which is revealed by one of the Fragments to be [[Bahamut (Final Fantasy XIII)|Bahamut's]] eidolith.

The meteor that Noel arrives to [[New Bodhum]] in is also a crystal. [[Atlas (Final Fantasy XIII-2)|Atlas]] is powered by a type of crystal. The [[Historia Crux]] utilizes crystal as a means of preserving the states of locations that have previously been visited, as completed locations bear the message "Time and memory, frozen in crystal".

There is a link between the deities and the crystals in the ''Fabula Nova Crystallis'' universe, as the fragment "[[Bhunivelze's Sleep]]" mentions that the crystals give birth to all things via the deities' wills and that the eternal dream world of the crystal lies within the Unseen Realm.

====''[[Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII]]''====
[[File:LR Crystal.png|thumb|left|A large crystal appears before the party.]]
[[Random encounter]]s sometimes transform into green crystals upon being defeated to signify dropping an ability for [[Lightning (Final Fantasy XIII)|Lightning]]. [[Soul seed]]s, the objects that form monsters, take the form of small purple crystals and appear within [[Chaos infusion]]s. Special merchants pay for gathered soul seeds. During a quest in [[Luxerion]] related to [[Oerba Dia Vanille|Vanille]], Lightning must find a crystal shard that Vanille uses to keep in contact with [[Oerba Yun Fang|Fang]].

In the [[Datalog (Final Fantasy XIII)|Datalog]], it is stated that [[Bhunivelze (character)|Bhunivelze's]] true form is an everlasting crystal. After the [[Apocalypse (Lightning Returns)|Apocalypse]], Lightning and her friends are faced by a large crystal in a void, which shatters and triggers the birth of the [[New world (Lightning Returns)|new world]] and releases the souls of humanity.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy XIV]]'' ===
[[File:XIV Crystal Quest.jpg|thumb|The adventurer finds a crystal in the [[Black Shroud]].]]
[[Aetheryte]] crystals are massive shards of crystallized [[Aether (Final Fantasy XIV)|aether]]ic mist, precisely cut and fused to arcane machinery. The origin of the technology is unknown (and is apparently wholly unnecessary beyond aesthetic purposes as [[beastmen|beastman]] tribes make use of aetheryte fashioned entirely of raw crystal) and aetheryte primarily serves as a means for the [[Warrior of Light (Final Fantasy XIV)|Warrior of Light]] to get from place to place.

[[Crystal (Final Fantasy XIV)|Elemental crystals and shards]] can also be gathered for fuel in item synthesis. Most crystals are aspected to one of six elements, but some can be drained of their elemental aspect, which are called deaspected crystals, or excessively aspects, called overaspected crystals.

[[Mor Dhona]] is littered with naturally occurring crystals as a side effect of the environmental damage caused by the [[Battle of Silvertear Skies]], as opposed to the enshrined gems seen elsewhere. Crystals as scenery is a common element in final or significant areas for much of the series.

[[File:Final Fantasy XIV ARR crystal.jpg|thumb|left|Hydaelyn's Mothercrystal.]]
Eorzeans' myths and legends extol that their world was created by the Mothercrystal, which became synonymous with [[Hydaelyn (character)|Hydaelyn]], an Elder Primal who serves as its protector and shows it in visions communicating with her chosen. The Mothercrystal is located deep within the depths of [[Source (Final Fantasy XIV)|the Source]], in truth merely a colossal crystal formed of aether crystallized in the depths of the [[aetherial sea]] under Hydaelyn's influence. Hydaelyn can bestow special "Crystals of Light" on certain individuals; the Warrior of Light obtains six of them through the course of the main scenario. These crystals act as a conduit for the blessing of Light. Hydaelyn later bestows the vast aether within the Mothercrystal to the members of the [[Scions of the Seventh Dawn]] so that they can use it to reach [[Meteion]], followed by [[Zenos Galvus]] consuming what remained of the Mothercrystal.

Four crystals can be seen during the animation of the [[Black Mage (Final Fantasy XIV)|Thaumaturge]] ability, [[Swiftcast]].{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy XV]]'' ===
{{Main|Crystal (Final Fantasy XV)}}
[[File:Ffxv_crystal.png|left|thumb|The Crystal of Lucis.]]
The Crystal is a powerful magical artifact in the world of [[Eos (Final Fantasy XV)|Eos]]. The Crystal's power is that of light and is a source of unmatched magical power. It is kept by the kingdom of [[Lucis]] and protected by the [[Kings of Lucis|line of Lucian kings]]. According to legend, the Crystal is of divine origin and was bestowed to humanity alongside the [[Ring of the Lucii]], which harnesses the Crystal's power for a chosen few. The ring itself holds a small crystal. A legend speaks of the [[True King|King of Light]], the one who will wield the full powers of the Crystal to save the world from darkness. The Crystal mythos in ''Final Fantasy XV'' incorporates many traditional ''Final Fantasy'' elements.

[[File:FFXV-Astral-Shard.png|thumb|A crystalline meteorite, as seen in the wilds of the Duscae region.]]
The [[Disc of Cauthess]] is a site where the remains of a [[Meteor of the Six|crystalline meteorite]] lie, said to have been caught by the [[Astral]] [[Titan (Final Fantasy XV)|Titan]] eons ago. The crystal meteorite burns with a blue light and the town of [[Lestallum]] uses shards of it as a power source.{{clear}}
===''[[Final Fantasy XVI]]''===
{{Main|Mothercrystal (Final Fantasy XVI)}}
Crystals in the land of [[Valisthea]] are mountainous monuments that bless their realms with aether. People revere and flock to them, using the aether to ease their lives. As the crystals are the power of the land, great wars have been waged over access to them, but an uneasy peace has prevailed for a long time until the coming of the [[Blight (Final Fantasy XVI)|Blight]].

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics]]'' ===
{{Quote|Gleaming jewels, left behind by living beings upon death, that harbor the power of the soul. They can impart vitality as well as the knowledge of the departed to those who touch them, and with their gentle light, illuminate the darkest places.|[[Terms (Tactics)|Terms]]}}
[[File:FFT Crystals.png|right]]
Crystals may appear when a defeated unit remains unconscious for three rounds (300 CT). They represent the condensed soul energy of the defeated unit. Living units may pick up these crystals to fully restore their [[HP (stat)|HP]] and [[MP (stat)|MP]]. If a human unit picks up the crystal formed from another human's soul, the living unit may choose instead to learn the abilities that the defeated unit had learned at no [[JP (Tactics)|JP]] cost. Once a unit's soul condenses into a crystal, its body disappears and it cannot be revived by any means, making the transformation into a crystal a form of [[wikipedia:permanent death|permanent death]].

The crystals of defeated human units are based on their color palette. The party and [[guest]]s (palette 00) have the teal-gray crystal, the [[Order of the Northern Sky]] units (palette 01) have the bright blue crystal, the [[Order of the Southern Sky]] units (palette 02) have the red crystal, the [[Corpse Brigade]]/[[Baert Trading Company]]/random battle units (palette 03) have the yellow crystal, and the [[Church of Glabados]] units (palette 04) have the purplish-gray crystal.

In [[Midlight's Deep (Tactics)|Midlight's Deep]], each blackout area can be lit by an unclaimed crystal. The area will be completely revealed when there are five crystals present.

The twelve [[Auracite (Tactics)|auracite]]s are crystalline stones of great power. The powers of [[Ivalice (Tactics)|Ivalice]] vie over their possession, with the foremost party being the [[Knights Templar|Temple Knights]] of the [[Church of Glabados]], who know of the Stones' relation to the [[Lucavi]] demons. There is also a hidden thirteenth auracite obtained from [[Elidibus (Tactics)|Elidibus]] on the tenth floor of Midlight's Deep. This stone represents [[Serpentarius]] the Serpent, but is simply an add to the original twelve.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics Advance]]'' ===
[[File:FFTA Crystal.png|thumb|A crystal.]]
The five crystals are the threads that bind the dream [[Ivalice (Tactics)|Ivalice]], made by the palace, and each one represents one of the races of Ivalice. Crystals exist in special folds in space called "seams". As the crystal's magic is beneficial to all of Ivalice, special means are being employed to protect them. This was once known in a theory, with one of the believers being [[Montblanc]]. This is confirmed when the [[clan]] has to fight the first guardian of the crystals, also known as [[Totema]], [[Famfrit (Tactics Advance)|Famfrit]].

[[Marche Radiuju|Marche's]] quest is to shatter the crystals to return home. To do this, he must defeat the Totema that guards each crystal. A sixth crystal is Queen [[Remedi]], the Li-Grim in her true form, and even when they are all destroyed, it takes the will of all of those from the old world to allow them to return to the [[St. Ivalice|real world]].

The classic four crystals of Fire, Water, Wind, and Earth appear in a group of optional subquests, known as "sigils". During these missions, each sigil must be obtained by defeating a "Falgabird" of the corresponding element: [[Marilith]] (Fire), [[Lich]] (Earth), [[Kraken]] (Water), and [[Tiamat (creature)|Tiamat]] (Wind). These Falgabirds are a reference to the original [[Four Fiends (Final Fantasy)|Four Fiends]]. Once the four sigils are obtained, two further missions can be completed to craft the Mind Ceffyl and the Body Ceffyl from them.{{clear}}

==== ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift]]'' ====
Crystals appear in certain quests/battles. When touched, the crystals allow the character to be transported to a different battlefield. Touching the crystals is usually required to complete missions they appear in.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics S]]'' ===
{{Section|Final Fantasy Tactics S}}

=== ''[[Crystal Defenders]]'' ===
The player defends crystals from numerous waves of enemies. In addition, there are [[Power Crystals]], which raise the abilities of nearby units.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Type-0]]'' ===
[[File:Vermilion-Bird-Crystal-Neutralized-Type0-HD.png|thumb|The Vermilion Bird Crystal.]]
{{Main|Crystal (Type series)}}
A Crystal is located in each peristylium of [[Orience]], bestowing the nation with a blessing and power to its citizens, representative of mankind's pursuits. Said to have been found long ago within their respective regions, they act as a means of political power, allowing their people to rule over their lands with a means of protection from invasion and to inspire hope.

The Crystals are sentient and their will is often expressed through a [[l'Cie]] of its choosing who are unable to oppose the Will of the Crystals. The people of Orience revere the Crystals for their power and, in return, the Crystals erase the personal memories associated with those who die among those who knew them. The Crystals are said to will for an equilibrium in the world, but their true purpose seems to be to compete for birthing [[Agito (term)|Agito]], culminating in the wars that ravage Orience.

The four Crystals of Orience are the [[Vermilion Bird Crystal]] of the [[Dominion of Rubrum]] that bestows the Power of Magic, the [[White Tiger Crystal]] of the [[Militesi Empire]] that bestows the Power of Weapons, the [[Azure Dragon Crystal]] of the [[Kingdom of Concordia]] that bestows the Power of the Dragon, and the [[Black Tortoise Crystal]] of the [[Lorican Alliance]] that bestows the Power of the Shield.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles]]'' ===
Large crystals can be found in every town and village. They protect people from the poisonous mist known as [[Miasma (term)|Miasma]] that plagues the world. However, the effect is temporary and, after a year, each town and village must send out [[Crystal Caravan (Crystal Chronicles)|Crystal Caravans]] to collect three drops of [[Myrrh]]. To collect the Myrrh, the Caravanners use a [[Crystal Chalice]], which not only can hold the Myrrh, but can protect the travelers from Miasma with its crystal for a short range.

A [[Carbuncle (Crystal Chronicles)|Carbuncle]] in [[Mag Mell]] reveals that the crystals protecting each village and city were originally part of a once [[Great Crystal (Crystal Chronicles)|Great Crystal]] that was shattered after being struck by a meteor that brought with it the [[Meteor Parasite]] that spread the Miasma.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Ring of Fates]]'' ====
[[File:RoF Giant Crystal.PNG|right|thumb|Crystal in Rela Cyel.]]
Crystals are an item for everyday life. [[Chelinka]] was born with a special crystal in her hand that she can only use when her twin brother, [[Yuri (Crystal Chronicles)|Yuri]], is around.

The [[Great Crystal (Crystal Chronicles)|Great Crystal]] holds the memories of the world. It is later revealed that use of the crystals alters the path of reality and destiny. When the crystals are used by the moontouched [[Lunite]]s, they turn crimson, whereas the crystals are normally blue.

Crystals found in towns and dungeons fully heal party members and also act as a save point and checkpoint.

RoF Crystal.png|Save Crystal in Story Mode.

</gallery>
{{clear}}

==== ''[[Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: My Life as a King]]'' ====
In [[Padarak]], a [[Great Crystal (Crystal Chronicles)#Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: My Life as a King|Crystal]] that appears within the Kingdom grants [[King Leo (Crystal Chronicles)|King Leo]] the power of [[Architek]], which allows him to rebuild his father's kingdom. To build new buildings, a type of crystal known as [[elementite]]s must be collected by Adventurers in dungeons. These elementites were once part of the main antagonist, the [[Darklord Craydall|Dark Lord]].

==== ''[[Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Echoes of Time]]'' ====
[[File:EoT Crystal.png|right|thumb|250px|Crystal.]]
Originally, Crystals were used to keep the air clean and bestow prosperity on the land. When an inventor, [[Larkeicus]], created machines that would allow the people to live a life of luxury (and for himself, immortality), Crystals were harvested as energy sources. As time passed, the crystals disappeared and the people became desperate for more, digging mines to uncover them.

One day, a large Crystal, the world's last remaining [[Crystal Core]], appeared in a small [[Village]]. Larkeicus located the last Crystal using his ring, while also searching around the globe for a new source of Crystals. The inventor found [[Sherlotta]] in the [[Forest (Echoes of Time)|Forest]] after killing the rest of the villagers. When the Crystal appeared in a forest pond, it infused itself to Sherlotta's soul, creating, presumably, a [[starsinger]]. Larkeicus could not take the Crystal, even though there was no one to stop him. The Crystal Core was a sort of negative Crystal, rendering Larkeicus' machines useless and sending his dynasty into ruins.

A thousand years later, Larkeicus realizes that the Crystals disappeared because of the shock waves from the future and prepares to stop the event from happening. When he activates the ruins, the Crystal Core shatters and is later repaired by the hero. In the game's final events, the Crystal Core is summoned to create the disturbance that made the Crystals disappear two millennia ago.

The hero is forced to shatter the Crystal and both Larkeicus and Sherlotta disappear in a blinding light. When arriving home, the hero throws the Crystal shard received from Sherlotta on his/her sixteenth birthday into the Crystal's pool. The next day, the once tiny Crystal begins to grow into one like the Crystal Core that appeared 2000 years ago.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: The Crystal Bearers]]'' ====
{{Quote|In the beginning there were the Four Crystals, and together they formed one Principle. Thus the world was created. The Four Crystals next created humanity in their own image, and presided over their destinies. Thus the Four Tribes were born: Lilty, Clavat, Selkie and we the Yuke.|Amidatelion}}
[[File:FFCCCB - Belle Flaunts Her Crystal idol.jpg|thumb|[[Belle]] and her crystal idol.]]
There are four Tribal Crystals, each representing a race, that form the "Crystal Principle", an ideal form of balance in the world. However, during the Crystal War, the Lilty destroyed the Yuke's Tribal Crystal, dooming the race to a place between Existence and Oblivion. The crystal shards were created from the Yuke's Crystal and served as a power source. The [[Crystal Idol]]s gather these shards to recreate the Yuke's Crystal.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Mystic Quest]]'' ===
[[File:FFMQ Light Crystal.png|left]]
[[File:MQCrystals.gif|thumb|right|Artwork of the four Crystals.]]
There are five Crystals, with four of them having their power drained by one of the [[Vile Four]]. [[Flamerus Rex]] drains the Crystal of Earth's power, rendering [[Level Forest]] and [[Foresta]] a decaying wasteland and turning most of the residents, including children, into old men and women. The [[Ice Golem (Mystic Quest)|Ice Golem's]] uses the Crystal of Water to send the [[Aquaria]] area into a permanent winter, the [[Dualhead Hydra]] causes earthquakes to become rampant around [[Fireburg]] using the Crystal of Fire, and [[Pazuzu (Mystic Quest)|Pazuzu]] causes violent windstorms using the Crystal of Wind.

In addition to these four crystals, the [[White (Mystic Quest character)|Crystal of Light]] appears to [[Benjamin]] as an old man offering cryptic advice. The Crystal of Light, in turn, may have been under the dark influences of the [[Dark King]], as it later shines at his throne when he is killed.{{clear}}

=== ''[[The Final Fantasy Legend]]'' ===
In the Japanese version, the spheres are called crystals. The spheres are needed in order to progress through the [[Tower (Legend)|Tower]] and they are gotten after the defeat of their respective Fiend. The spheres are used to unlock the sealed door that will allow the party to travel further up the floors of the Tower. Sei-Ryu created numerous fake spheres in order to protect the real one from being stolen from him. The Chinese writing on the spheres is Xuan (dark), Qing (blue-green), Bai (white), and Zhu (red).

=== ''[[Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light]]'' ===
{{Quote|The world cannot be allowed to fall into darkness! Heroes of Light, set forth on your journey!|The Crystal}}
[[File:FFT4HoL Crystal.png|right|200px]]
The Crystal appears before [[Brandt]], [[Jusqua]], [[Yunita]], and [[Aire]] and dubs them the [[Warriors of Light#Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light|Heroes of Light]]. Upon their first meeting, it warns them of the upcoming darkness. It will also grant them [[job system#Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light|crowns]] after they help various people and/or towns. The darkness encroaches even the souls of men and those who succumb to desire lose all faith. The Crystal wants the Heroes of Light to shine the light on their hearts and drive the darkness away, but those who believe in the Light will never know terror's blight.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Brave Exvius]]'' ===
Crystals contain [[vision]]s and [[Hess' Eight Sages]] were sealed inside large crystals.
{{Section|Final Fantasy Brave Exvius}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Dimensions]]'' ===
The world's most vital crystal lies within the nation of [[Lux (Dimensions)|Lux]]. Upon its shattering, the world itself became divided into one of light and one of darkness and its shards scattered throughout the world.

Amongst the [[Warriors of Light]] and the [[Warriors of Darkness]] who travel in the separated worlds in search of the shards of the world's crystal, they also bestow upon the parties the powers of different warrior [[job system|classes]] and are gained from people of different walks of life.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy Dimensions II]]'' ====
[[File:FFLTnS artwork.jpg|thumb|Crystal.]]
Crystals make an appearance. Signet crystals allow the player to use summoned creatures.
{{Section|Final Fantasy Dimensions II}}
{{clear}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Explorers]]'' ===
[[File:FFE-Field.jpg|thumb|The Great Crystal, towering over the landscape.]]
Crystals are said to be the receptacles for the energy of the stars. The most powerful is the Great Crystal, said to be the source of all life. The Great Crystal bestowed the people of the world with souls that could evolve over time and develop a civilization. Humanity begun to use crystals to advance their civilization and, when the island of [[Amostra]] rises from the sea carrying large crystal reserves, people see the island as an opportunity and [[Explorer (character)|Explorers]] head to the island to retrieve them. The crystals across the island are guarded by summoned monsters, which the Explorers must fight.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Dissidia Final Fantasy (2008)|Dissidia Final Fantasy]]'' ===
[[File:Dissidia Final Fantasy Crystals.png|right|200px|The ten crystals.]]
There are ten Crystals, each one representing one of the first ten games of the series. Each Crystal is somehow reflective of its original game or its representative character, such as [[Cloud Strife (Dissidia PSP)|Cloud's]] Crystal being a piece of a Materia, [[Zidane Tribal (Dissidia PSP)|Zidane's]] Crystal being the Crystal featured in the ''Final Fantasy IX'' logo, and [[Tidus (Dissidia PSP)|Tidus']] Crystal being a sphere.

These Crystals, later revealed to hold a tenth of [[Cosmos (Dissidia)|Cosmos']] power, had to be obtained by its respective Warrior of Cosmos by asserting their true desires to fight for what they believe in. To this end, their respective enemies challenge their beliefs, wishing to speed along the manifestation of the Crystals as part of a plot to destroy Cosmos. When all ten Crystals have been recovered, the player can access the final stage and confront the final boss, [[Chaos (Dissidia)|Chaos]]. After he is defeated, the Warriors of Cosmos each depart back to their own world, taking their Crystal with them.

[[Emperor Mateus (Dissidia PSP)|The Emperor]] is stated to possess several Dark Crystals as a result of [[Jecht (Dissidia PSP)|Jecht]], a former Warrior of Cosmos, manifesting them, but with their allegiance being to Chaos since he was brought to the side of discord. These Dark Crystals are not seen in-game, although it is known that with their power, the Emperor could survive the destruction of [[World B|the World]] and rule it after the Gods killed each other.

The [[manikin]]s that serve as the basic foes also appear to be living creatures made entirely of crystal.

Also, the Crystal from ''Final Fantasy V'' makes a cameo as a tutor in the in-game manuals.

==== ''[[Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy]]'' ====
The player witnesses Cosmos granting her power to her warriors, telling them that after they fight enough battles, this power will manifest as a Crystal. It is also during this cycle that the Emperor arranges for Jecht to become a Warrior of Chaos to manifest the Dark Crystals.

The [[Report (Dissidia 012)|Reports]], which go into detail on the backstory for ''Dissidia's'' world, explain that the manikins are living crystal ore recovered from [[The Void (term)|The Void]] that shapeshift to take on the forms of others.

=== ''[[Theatrhythm Final Fantasy]]'' ===
The Music Crystal is the source of music and harmony in the world, existing in the space between Cosmos and Chaos called Rhythm. When the forces of chaos disrupt the Music Crystal's energy, the heroes embark on a journey to energize it with [[Rhythmia]] and restore its light.

The player can also collect crystal shards by playing [[Dark Note]]s and reaching certain Rhythmia milestones.

Obtaining eight crystal shards of the same color will unlock a new character:
* Yellow - Cid Haze
* Indigo - Locke Cole
* Orange - Vivi
* Scarlet - Ashe
* Silver - Minwu
* Green - Rydia
* Crimson - Faris
* Red - Aerith
* Turquoise - Yuna
* Gold - Princess Sarah
* Gray - Seifer
* Purple - Prishe
* White - Snow
* Rainbow - Cosmos
* Navy - Kain
* Black - Sephiroth

=== ''[[Theatrhythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call]]'' ===
The Music Crystal returns, functioning the same as it did in the previous game. Crystal shards also return, but their function has been altered. Rather than collecting a different color for each character, five to six characters are designated to one color (excluding Black shards) and, with the number of shards reduced, makes unlocking characters easier. In addition, the default characters that are not chosen as the player's initial party can be later unlocked through crystal shards.

Characters that require four shards to unlock:
* Red - Warrior of Light, Bartz, Zidane, Lightning, Cosmos, Zack
* Indigo - Firion, Terra, Tidus, Y'shtola, Yuna #2, Serah
* Yellow - Onion Knight, Cloud, Shantotto, Benjamin, Ramza, Ace
* Green - Cecil, Squall, Vaan, Ciaran, Tifa #2, Lightning #2

Characters that require six shards to unlock:
* Peach - Princess Sarah, Rydia, Aerith, Yuna, Snow, Rikku
* Purple - Minwu, Faris, Seifer, Prishe, Machina, Noel
* Orange - Cid, Locke, Vivi, Ashe, Agrias
* Turquoise - Kain, Celes, Rinoa, Auron, Balthier, Paine
* White - Lenna, Tifa, Garnet, Aphmau, Hope, Rem
* Silver - Galuf, Barret, Eiko, Lilisette, Vanille
* Gold - Edge, Edgar, Laguna, Jecht, Fran

Character that requires eight shards to unlock:
* Black - Sephiroth

=== ''[[Stranger of Paradise Final Fantasy Origin]]'' ===
[[Jack Garland|Jack]], [[Ash (Stranger of Paradise)|Ash]], [[Jed]], [[Neon (Stranger of Paradise)|Neon]], and [[Sophia (Stranger of Paradise)|Sophia]] all possess a dark-colored egg-shaped crystal that seemingly draws them to destroy Chaos and restore the elemental Crystals. After defeating a strong enemy, such as a Fiend, the crystal may absorb the residue darkness and unlock some of the user's memories, allowing them to recall some of their past.

Each crystal is a [[Lufenian]] memory storage device that allows [[Stranger (Stranger of Paradise)|Stranger]]s to collect their memories and bring them into the next time loop, making it easier to remember their real mission. In one of the earlier iterations of the cycle, Jack entrusted his original Dark Crystal to [[Sarah (Stranger of Paradise)|Princess Sarah]] to use it as a failsafe to remember his real task to stop the Lufenians' influence over [[Cornelia (Stranger of Paradise)|Cornelia]].

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Airborne Brigade]]'' ===
[[File:Crystal Brigade.png|thumb|Obtaining abilities from a Crystal.]]
Crystals contain abilities made available for players to peruse, use, enhance, sell, or to destroy their enemies. Crystals containing abilities may be obtained from varying [[chocobo]]s, usually of the Yellow, Black, and White variety, although mutations such as that of a red feathering do tend to exist and, as such, result in rarer ability gains. They are also involved with the process of boosting an ability's initial limit, evolving the ability past its prime within the Crystal chamber.
{{Section|Final Fantasy Airborne Brigade}}

The Crystal is mentioned in the prologue, but it does not appear within the game.

=== ''[[Chocobo's Dungeon 2]]'' ===
[[File:CD2 Crystal.png|right|thumb|A Crystal.]]
{{Section|Chocobo's Dungeon 2}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Fables: Chocobo Tales]]'' ===
Five Crystals appear and are connected to different elements and guarded by different [[List of summons|Summon Creatures]]. The Red Crystal sitting atop the volcano Mt. Magma has power over Fire and is protected by [[Phoenix]]. The Green Crystal of Earth rests in the forest, under [[Unicorn (creature)|Unicorn's]] watchful eye. The Blue Crystal hidden in the underwater shrine controls Water and has [[Leviathan]] as its guardian. The Yellow Crystal stationed at the highest floor of the Technolith is aligned with the power of Light and is under [[Ramuh]]'s care. The final crystal, the Black Crystal, was created by [[Bebuzzu]] to bolster the powers of darkness and chaos by feeding off of the negativity within the hearts of living creatures.

[[Irma]] uses this crystal to drain the others and then feeds the energy to Bebuzzu, who, in turn, is transformed by each power. At the end of the game, he uses the fully powered Black Crystal to travel to the world of darkness as he tries to revert the universe to its original form—[[The Void (term)|The Void]]. A backstory for the Crystals is given in the story [[Legend of the Crystals (Chocobo Tales)|Legend of the Crystals]].

[[File:JaneCrystal.jpg|left|thumb|200px|Jane's crystal pendant.]]
[[Jane Proudfoot]] possesses a green crystal as a pendant attached to the knife on her Anti SB Mechanized Infantry Protection System armor.{{clear}}

== Non-''Final Fantasy'' guest appearances ==
=== ''{{KHWiki|Kingdom Hearts II}}'' ===
The {{KHWiki|Struggle Trophy}}, awarded to the winner of the Struggle in {{KHWiki|Twilight Town}}, features four unique crystals of red, blue, green, and yellow. {{KHWiki|Mickey Mouse}} gives {{KHWiki|Sora}} a bag containing a blue crystal that came from the Struggle Trophy in the {{KHWiki|Simulated Twilight Town}}.

=== ''{{KHWiki|Kingdom Hearts III}}'' ===
Master Xehanort is stated by Mickey Mouse to have "crystallized" Kairi as an "insurance policy." This may be a reference to the crystallization process of the ''[[Fabula Nova Crystallis: Final Fantasy]]'' titles.

During the initial unwinnable battle against the secret boss of the ''Re Mind'' downloadable content, Sora is crystallized following his defeat.

=== ''[[Bravely Default|Bravely]]'' series ===
[[File:BDFF Screenshot Crystal.jpg|right|200px|thumb|The Wind Crystal.]]
The ''Bravely'' games pay homage to the four elemental crystals from ''Final Fantasy''. There are four crystals representing Fire, Water, Wind, and Earth that act as the balancing force for the world of {{BravelyWiki|Luxendarc}} and each of its parallel counterparts, ruling over worldly elemental phenomena of their respective element. In the {{BravelyWiki|Crystal Orthodoxy}}, the crystals are objects of worship.

Each crystal is tended and prayed to by a vestal to ensure the stability of a crystal's power. Without the presence of a {{BravelyWiki|vestal}} or if the crystal is improperly managed, disasters will occur in its reigning region. Overstimulating the crystals can cause the elements they are linked with to behave erratically. When the crystals are threatened by the taint of darkness, the vestals perform rites to purify them, though a crystal can become corrupted to the point of impurity.

While the crystals can be destroyed, as long as their core—separate from the main crystal—remains intact, they will grow back to their original size and power using the prayers of humanity, although this process can take 5,000 years. Each crystal's core is {{BravelyWiki|Agnès Oblige|Agnès'}} pendant, which was bestowed to her by {{BravelyWiki|Sage Yulyana}}, who obtained it from the angel that resembled Agnès in his past.

Crystals also provide a link between parallel versions of Luxendarc. The {{BravelyWiki|Holy Pillar}} is a divine occurrence that emerges at the south-east of Luxendarc after all four crystals have been awakened. In the Crystal Orthodoxy, it is thought that praying to the Holy Pillar will purge the world from darkness. When a Holy Pillar emerges, it actually creates an opening of that world to another world parallel to it. {{BravelyWiki|Airy}} used the opportunity to weave each world together for {{BravelyWiki|Ouroboros (Bravely Default)|Ouroboros}}, the mastermind behind a plan to destroy all worlds and invade the {{BravelyWiki|Celestial Realm}}.{{clear}}

=== ''Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars'' ===
The four Crystals make a cameo as guardians of Culex. Each one have high-powered elemental spells corresponding with their element—the Fire Crystal uses fire attacks, the Water Crystal uses ice attacks, the Earth Crystal uses earth attacks, and the Wind Crystal uses thunder attacks. Culex is actually believed to have been based on bosses in the ''Final Fantasy'' series.

=== ''Crystal Conquest'' ===
[[File:Crystal Conquest - Crystal.png|50px|right]]
Massive crystals appears in this Japan-only, free-to-play browser game. The player has to destroy the enemy's crystal. Collecting one hundred crystal shards will allow the player to summon a summoned monster.{{clear}}

=== ''[[Mario Sports Mix]]'' ===
The four crystals appear in the game as Sports Crystals, which are awarded to the player for completing tournaments.

== Behind the scenes ==
[[Hironobu Sakaguchi]] attributes the inclusion of crystals in the original ''Final Fantasy'' to designer [[Koichi Ishii]].<ref name = "1up">{{ref|id= 1up | year = 2011 | month = 12 | day = 21 | first = Kevin | last = Gifford | entry = Hironobu Sakaguchi on Final Fantasy I's Roller-Coaster Development | title = [[Wikipedia:1Up Network|1UP.com]] | brokenlink = true | url = http://www.1up.com/news/hironobu-sakaguchi-final-fantasy-roller-coaster | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160305021100/http://www.1up.com/news/hironobu-sakaguchi-final-fantasy-roller-coaster | archive-date = 21 September 2013| access-date = 1 July 2022}}</ref> Ishii has stated that a major theme in the game was that the world exists because of the elemental forces of nature and ''Final Fantasy'' explored the relationship between these elements.<ref name = "retronauts">{{ref | id=retronauts | year = 2017 | month = 6 | day = 22 | first = Jeremy | last = Parish | entry = Ever Oasis producer Koichi Ishii on building on (and standing apart from) Secret of Mana | title = [[Wikipedia:Retronauts|Retronauts]] | url = https://retronauts.com/article/411/ever-oasis-producer-koichi-ishii-on-building-on-and-standing-apart-from-secret-of-mana | access-date = 1 July 2022}}</ref> The idea of certain enemies being resistant or weak to elemental attacks was taken from ''Dungeons & Dragons'', as gameplay designer [[Akitoshi Kawazu]] believed that the idea made sense and was something not done in Japanese RPGs before.<ref name = "saga">{{ref | id = saga | year1 = 2012 | month1 = 10 | year2 = 2017 | month2 = 11 | day2 = 13 | first = Jeremy |last = Parish | entry = Akitoshi Kawazu on the origins of SaGa's insanity | title = 1Up'', republished by'' Retronauts| url = https://retronauts.com/article/670/akitoshi-kawazu-on-the-reasoning-behind-sagas-insanity | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190819184025/https://retronauts.com/article/670/akitoshi-kawazu-on-the-reasoning-behind-sagas-insanity | archive-date = 24 June 2017 | access-date = 1 July 2022 }}</ref> This grew into the idea of the creatures of the world being tied to the four elements and the crystals represented the power of those elements.<ref name = "portal site">{{ref | id = portal site | year = 2020 | month = 5 | day = 1 | author = Square Enix | entry =  FINAL FANTASY III 30th Anniversary Special Interview Vol.2  | title = Final Fantasy Portal Site | url = https://na.finalfantasy.com/topics/176 | access-date = 1 July 2022 | link = Final Fantasy Portal App}}</ref> 

During development of ''Final Fantasy II'', some employees at Square were hesitant to make it a numbered sequel if it was set in a new world and it was agreed to retain some elements of the first game's setting to appeal to its fans. [[Kenji Terada]], the scenario writer for the first three ''Final Fantasy'' games, has said that it was his idea to keep the crystals as part of the setting, as crystals are a common idea in fantasy fiction, and he thought that they would be a good recurring theme to have if ''Final Fantasy'' became a larger franchise; the concept of crystals could be a "keyword" that future games explored in different ways.<ref name = "shmuplations">{{ref | id = shmuplations | year1 = 1988 | year2 = 2015 | year3 = 2021 | month3 = 12 | day3 = 29| author = BlackOak | entry = Kenji Terada – 1988 Developer Interview | title = shmuplations.com''. Original interviews published in ''Famicom Tsūshin'' (1988) and ''cakes.mu'' (2015)''&hairsp;| url = https://shmuplations.com/kenjiterada/ | access-date = 1 July 2022 }}</ref>
